maria_cust: Hey, prod is suddenly getting 401s from Redwood after a config-only deploy. Error body returns {\"error\":\"invalid_api_key\", \"message\":\"API key invalid or expired\"}. We rotated keys last night but nothing else changed. Anyone seen this?

jordan_support: Sorry you hit that — can you paste the exact curl you ran (sanitized), and whether the app uses env var, k8s secret, or a secrets manager? Also include the first 8 and last 4 chars of the key (no full key).

maria_cust: We're using a k8s secret populated from our password manager. Here's the sanitized curl I ran from one of the pods:

```
curl -i \n  -H "Authorization: Api-Key •••••••••••" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat/completions \n  -d '{"model":"redwood-chat-1","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}] }'
```

I replaced the key with bullets rather than the real value because I don't want to paste it in channel.

jordan_support: That bullets thing is the clue — some password managers / browser extensions copy the field mask (• • •) instead of the underlying secret when you use the quick-copy action. Can you check length on the pod? Run:

```bash
echo -n "$REDWOOD_API_KEY" | wc -c
```

If it returns a very small number (like 6 or 10) that's the masked copy. Real Redwood API keys are ~36-60 chars.

maria_cust: Running that now... it prints `6`. Oof. That explains the invalid_api_key. We thought the k8s secret had the new key but it looks like the masked value got pushed.

lee_engineer: We ran into this before with the team using the browser extension for 1Password/Bitwarden. Two quick fixes: 1) open the vault entry, click reveal/show, then copy; 2) in the pod/container check the raw secret value before redeploying. Also check your CI step — if the secret sync job uses the quick-copy, it will persist the masked value everywhere.

maria_cust: Found the bad commit in the secret-sync job — it's copying from the extension's field instead of the revealed value. Updating the job to source from the CLI export fixes it. I'll rotate the key again and push the corrected secret.

secrets-bot: rotation event: service=secrets-sync user=maria_cust env=prod rotated_key_id=sk_live_8xYz*** at 2026-03-17T14:03:15Z

maria_cust: Redeployed with the correct value (checked length = 45). Running the same curl now...

```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Api-Key sk_live_8xYz...9Qf" -H "Content-Type: application/json" https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat/completions -d '{"model":"redwood-chat-1","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"ok"}] }'
```

Response: HTTP/1.1 200 OK

Thanks team, all good now.

jordan_support: Great — glad that was it. For follow-ups: 1) add a length check in your secret-sync CI (fail if < 30 chars); 2) add a config note to the repo reminding to use "reveal" when copying; 3) consider using the provider's CLI token export to avoid extension quirks. Marking as resolved. :white_check_mark:
